title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
summary: Connect points on a plane with the least total Manhattan distance so that every point is reachable from every other.

tests.explain: One point is already connected: cost 0.

hints: You are asked for the cheapest set of connections that links every point into one network. Such a cheapest connected network never contains a cycle: it is a minimum spanning tree.
Build every possible edge with cost |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|, sort the edges by cost, and add them cheapest first (Kruskal). An edge is only useful if its two endpoints are not yet connected.
Track connectivity with union-find. For each edge in sorted order, if find(a) !== find(b) then union them and add the cost. Stop after n - 1 edges have been added.

complexity.time: O(n² log n): n² edges are generated and sorted
complexity.space: O(n²) for the edge list plus O(n) for union-find
